citation: PMID 40707480 (Ren, Zhao, Chen, Ou, Feng 2025, Nat Commun 16:6816, doi 10.1038/s41467-025-62152-8; PDB 9IKB)
claim_tested: That a partial kinesin-2 stalk and tail structure can resolve which KLP-11 residues pair with KLP-20 and which bind KAP-1
key_finding: KAP-1 is an elongated superhelix with a central groove and a C-terminal helical (CTH) hook; the KLP-11 and KLP-20 tails fold together into the groove, and the hetero-pairing trigger sequences preceding the tails form an intertwined heterodimer that co-captures the CTH hook. Interface mutations disrupt the holoenzyme and impair IFT.
context: C. elegans KLP-11, KLP-20, KAP-1 fragments, crystallography plus in vivo IFT assays
confidence_and_limitations: High for the modelled region. The construct covers KLP-11 537-721 only (17.1% of the protein) and KLP-20 531-624 (13.5%). No motor domain, neck linker, neck coil or stalk CC1 is present. Resolution 3.54 A limits side-chain placement, so individual contact assignments are leads, not settled facts.

claim_tested: That the KLP-20-pairing residues and the KAP-1-binding residues of KLP-11 can be separated
key_finding: 61 KLP-11 residues contact KLP-20 and 54 contact KAP-1, with 18 in both sets. The coiled-coil and beta-hairpin block 539-591 contacts KLP-20 only; 711-721 contacts KAP-1 only; 644-710 is a dual interface. Buried surface: KLP-11:KLP-20 2540 A2, KLP-11:KAP-1 2486 A2, KLP-20:KAP-1 1288 A2.
context: Re-analysis of deposited coordinates; 5.0 A heavy-atom contact cut-off, Shrake-Rupley SASA with 1.4 A probe
confidence_and_limitations: Direct computation on experimental coordinates. Contact lists at 3.54 A inherit the model's side-chain uncertainty. Crystal packing was not separately excluded, although the three interfaces are all large and the two largest exceed 2400 A2.

claim_tested: That the heterodimer is asymmetric in its KAP-1 engagement
key_finding: KLP-11 buries 1.91x more surface on KAP-1 than KLP-20 does (2486 vs 1288 A2), and KLP-11 711-721 touches KAP-1 exclusively while KLP-20 makes no contact of any kind beyond residue 624.
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate to high. The KLP-20 construct ends at 646 and is modelled only to 624, so part of the difference could reflect construct design rather than biology. The direction of the asymmetry matches the longer B-type tail seen in sequence (see next rows).

claim_tested: That the coiled-coil heptad register differs between the two subunits
key_finding: Crick-style core assignment gives KLP-11 a/d core L546 I550 V553 L557 K560 V564 I568 and KLP-20 core V533 M536 I540 L543 L547 N550. One core layer is polar and asymmetric: KLP-11 K560 against KLP-20 N550, closest heavy-atom distance 3.98 A. By alignment the vertebrate equivalents are KIF3B K583 and KIF3A Q588.
context: Same structure plus pairwise alignment to O15066 and Q9Y496
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. The core assignment is geometric and reproducible, but a buried charge-plus-amide layer at 3.54 A is a lead for a heterospecificity determinant, not proof. The vertebrate equivalence is alignment-based with no vertebrate structure to check it.

claim_tested: That the neck linker is a site of KLP-11 / KLP-20 asymmetry
key_finding: The 11-mer TLRYANRAKNI is identical in KLP-11, KLP-20, KIF3B and KIF3A. The 17-residue windows differ only at conservative positions. Neck linker plus neck coil identity is 37.0% (worm pair) and 44.7% (human pair), but within the linker proper it is 100%.
confidence_and_limitations: High for the sequence fact. It does not exclude asymmetry in neck linker docking kinetics, which sequence cannot report.

claim_tested: That KLP-11 is the B-type (KIF3B-like) subunit and KLP-20 the A-type
key_finding: Motor-domain identity: KLP-11/KIF3B 72.2%, KLP-20/KIF3A 69.1%, against KLP-11/KIF3A 62.1% and KLP-20/KIF3B 62.6%. KLP-11 and KLP-20 are only 58.2% identical in the motor domain, less than either is to its vertebrate ortholog.
confidence_and_limitations: High. Orthology direction is unambiguous by reciprocal best identity.

claim_tested: That an autoinhibitory tail element lies on one subunit rather than the other
key_finding: Pfam PF32951 (Kinesin-2-like, C-terminal domain) is annotated once in each subunit: KLP-11 545-592, KLP-20 536-584, KIF3B 568-617, KIF3A 573-622. The element is duplicated, not subunit-specific.
confidence_and_limitations: High for the annotation. Presence of a domain in both subunits does not mean both contribute equally to autoinhibition.

claim_tested: That the autoinhibitory element can be assigned to one subunit from the stalk structure
key_finding: Subunit-specific interactions between the motor domains and the C-terminal coiled-coil domains plus adjacent tail beta-hairpin motifs stabilise the autoinhibited state, and these same C-terminal regions are required for stable heterodimerisation.
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate to high for the vertebrate pair. The regions are shared between autoinhibition and assembly, so a structure of the assembled tail cannot separate the two functions. One half of the autoinhibitory contact (the motor domains) is absent from 9IKB.

citation: PMID 40497557 (Chen, Guo, Zhu, Xie, Zhou, Ou 2025)
claim_tested: Where kinesin-2 autoregulation is controlled in C. elegans
key_finding: NEKL-3 phosphorylates a flexible elbow between the two coiled-coil domains of OSM-3; the phospho-dead mutation gives constitutive motility in vitro, and both phospho-dead and phospho-mimic knock-ins shorten sensory cilia.
context: C. elegans OSM-3 (homodimeric kinesin-2), in vitro and in vivo
confidence_and_limitations: High for OSM-3. OSM-3 is a different kinesin-2, so this does not transfer directly to KLP-11. It locates the regulatory switch at the elbow, which in KLP-11 is residues 502-544 and is 81% absent from 9IKB.

claim_tested: Whether regulation of kinesin-II resides in the subunits themselves
key_finding: JBTS-26 competes with kinesin-II for binding to IFT-B subunit OSM-5/IFT88 and displaces kinesin-II from IFT particles; loss of JBTS-26 lets kinesin-II invade the distal cilium.
confidence_and_limitations: High for the phenotype. Shows an external regulator of kinesin-II localization, an alternative to a subunit-intrinsic regulatory element.

key_finding: Proposed a KLP-11 / OSM-3 / KAP-1 heterotrimer on sequence-homology grounds.
confidence_and_limitations: Low for the pairing claim, now superseded: the holoenzyme pairs KLP-11 with KLP-20 (PMID 40707480). Flagged because annotations derived from this paper may still assert an OSM-3 partnership.

claim_tested: What klp-11 loss does in the animal
key_finding: nphp-2 and the doublet-region genes arl-13, klp-11 and unc-119 are redundantly required for ciliogenesis; nphp-2 plus klp-11 form one genetic module.
context: C. elegans amphid and phasmid sensory cilia
confidence_and_limitations: High for the genetic interaction. This is a downstream ciliary phenotype, not evidence about subunit asymmetry or autoregulation.

citation: AlphaFold DB v6 (Q19633, Q965T6, O15066, Q9Y496)
claim_tested: Whether the unmodelled regions can substitute for the missing structure
key_finding: Helix assignment places the first post-motor helix at KLP-11 351-379, KLP-20 339-365, KIF3B 354-386, KIF3A 354-379. KLP-11 723-782 has pLDDT below 50 and is predicted disordered.
confidence_and_limitations: Monomer models give element boundaries but no inter-subunit register and no autoinhibited conformation. They cannot stand in for a full-length holoenzyme structure.
